class.name: BarkDetail3D
class.brief_description: Loose bark pieces as real geometry on the tree trunks near the camera.
class.description: Close-up bark: the pieces a trunk's bark sheds, laid on the stem as instanced geometry over the displaced relief of the trunk's nearest LOD (bark as elements on a surface, after Pixar's "Elemental Bark"). Each bark family has its own kind of piece: plates lifting at their lower edge (pines), small scales (holm oak, blackthorn), flakes curling out at one end (flaking bark), and torn strips of paper bark rolling outward (birches). Smooth, furrowed and cork bark shed none: their relief is the stem's own geometry. Pieces lie on the trunk mesh's real bark surface, at the outermost bark in each cell of a grid round the stem, and take the stem's vertex colour, bark texture and normal map; their undersides and broken edges show the family's inner bark. Plates and scales only sit on plate tops, never in furrows. Each family uses 8 shapes, picked per piece with its own size, spin and texture offset, so neighbours do not repeat. Trunks come from [member vegetation] ([method VegetationField3D.get_trunks_near]) or from [method set_trunks]. A trunk's pieces are the same every time it comes near. Each family is drawn out to where its pieces are still [member detail_pixels] tall on screen, up to [member max_reach]. New trunks are placed on a worker thread; the main thread only gathers trunks and fills the buffers. Pieces are ray traced with the scene. A trunk mesh with a [code]tree_bark_profile[/code] meta (from [method make_bark_profile], which [TreeGenerator] stores when it builds the mesh) costs nothing to read. Without it, the bark surface is read back from the GPU once per mesh, which stalls the render thread.

method.name: get_bark_kind
method.description: The bark family of a [TreeGenerator] preset.

method.name: get_piece_size
method.description: The mean size of a bark family's pieces, in metres ([code]0[/code] for families that shed none).

method.name: get_reach
method.description: Metres from the camera a bark family's pieces are drawn out to: where they are [member detail_pixels] tall, at most [member max_reach].

method.name: get_trunk_count
method.description: Trunks near the camera now, with or without pieces.

method.name: get_update_msec_mean
method.description: The mean main-thread time of an update, in milliseconds.

method.name: get_update_msec_worst
method.description: The worst main-thread time of an update, in milliseconds.

method.name: is_placing
method.description: Whether a worker is placing new trunks' pieces.

method.name: is_sync
method.description: Whether pieces are placed on the main thread (see [method set_sync]).

method.name: make_bark_profile
method.description: A trunk mesh's bark surface binned round its stem, for the mesh's [code]tree_bark_profile[/code] meta: [param vertices] and [param colors] are the bark surface's arrays, [param colliders] its [code]tree_colliders[/code] meta. Covers the stem's first 4.2 m. Returns [code][header, radii, colours][/code]: a [PackedFloat32Array] (cells round, rows, row step in metres), the outermost bark radius in each cell in metres, and a [PackedByteArray] of each cell's mean vertex colour (RGB, 0 to 2 in 8 bits).

method.name: set_sync
method.description: Places new trunks' pieces on the main thread, at once (tests).

method.name: set_trunks
method.description: Trunks to dress instead of [member vegetation]'s, as dictionaries in the form [method VegetationField3D.get_trunks_near] returns, optionally with [code]"mesh"[/code] (the trunk's [Mesh]) for its bark surface, colour and material.

method.name: update_now
method.description: Gathers the trunks near the camera, places new ones and drops those out of reach, now rather than on the next update.

members.member: Scales the number of pieces a square metre of stem.
A family's pieces are drawn out to where they are this many pixels tall on screen.
Metres up the trunk pieces are laid, from 0.3 m (above the root flare). At most 4 m.
The farthest any piece is drawn from the camera, in metres.
The screen height in pixels [member detail_pixels] is measured against; [code]0[/code] uses the viewport's.
The node whose position the pieces follow; empty follows the current camera.

constants.constant: A plate lifting from the stem at its lower edge.
A thin flake curling out at one end.
A strip of paper bark rolling outward round the stem.
